name: World Cup
hook: Soccer's quadrennial spectacle — the trophy, Brazil, and the finals everyone remembers.

facts.label: 1930 in Uruguay
facts.statement: The first World Cup began July 13, 1930, in Montevideo; 13 countries competed and Uruguay won.

facts.label: the Jules Rimet Cup
facts.statement: The Jules Rimet Cup, named for FIFA's three-decade president, was replaced by the current trophy in 1974.

facts.label: Brazil
facts.statement: Brazil is the only country to play in every World Cup and has won it five times, starting with Pelé's 1958 title.

facts.label: host nations
facts.statement: Japan and South Korea co-hosted in 2002, and the United States hosted in 1994.

facts.label: France 2018
facts.statement: France beat Croatia 4-2 in 2018, the highest-scoring final in 52 years; Croatia's president, Kolinda Grabar-Kitarović, celebrated in the stands.

facts.label: Brandi Chastain
facts.statement: Brandi Chastain's winning kick in Pasadena gave the U.S. the 1999 Women's World Cup, then she tore off her shirt; the U.S. has won the most women's titles.

facts.label: South Africa 2010
facts.statement: The 2010 tournament in South Africa is remembered for the vuvuzela and Paul the "psychic" octopus, who went 6-for-6 on his picks.
